tool.name: Triqler
tool.description: protein quantification and differential abundance with integrated error rates
tool.command: ## Triqler writes its peptide table next to the input and treats inputs ending ## in .pqr.tsv as peptide tables, so stage the input under a fixed name. #if $input.is_of_type('tabular.gz'): gunzip -c '$input' > input.tsv && #else ln -s '$input' input.tsv && #end if mkdir results posteriors && #if str($protein_name_separator) == 'auto': ## Each separator setting silently misreads the other style of shared ## peptide, so detect it: extra columns after the proteins column mean tab, ## a semicolon inside it means semicolon (OpenMS and DIA-NN converters). separator=\$(awk -F '\t' ' NR == 1 { col = 7; for (i = 1; i <= NF; i++) if (\$i == "linkPEP") col = 10; next } NF > col { print "tab"; exit } \$col ~ /;/ { print "semicolon"; exit } ' input.tsv) && #else separator='$protein_name_separator' && #end if if [ "\$separator" = semicolon ]; then set -- --protein_name_separator ';'; else set --; fi && triqler --out_file results/proteins.tsv --fold_change_eval $fold_change_eval --decoy_pattern='$decoy_pattern' "\$@" --missing_value_prior '$missing_value_prior' --min_samples $min_samples --num_threads "\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1}" $output_options.write_protein_posteriors $output_options.write_group_posteriors $output_options.write_fold_change_posteriors input.tsv && ## With exactly two conditions Triqler writes an unsuffixed file; give it the ## same name it would get with more conditions so the collection is uniform. if [ -f results/proteins.tsv ]; then mv results/proteins.tsv results/proteins.1vs2.tsv; fi && ## Triqler's csv writer ends lines with CRLF, which leaves a stray carriage ## return in the last column for downstream tabular tools. for f in results/*.tsv posteriors/*.tsv input.tsv.pqr.tsv; do if [ -f "\$f" ]; then tr -d '\r' < "\$f" > "\$f.lf" && mv "\$f.lf" "\$f" || exit 1; fi; done

param.name: input
param.label: Triqler input table
param.help: PSM or precursor table with the columns run, condition, charge, searchScore, intensity, peptide and proteins, for example from OpenMS TriqlerConverter. It must be tab-delimited, even when Galaxy labels it csv. Intensities must not be log transformed and decoy entries must be included.

param.label: Log2 fold change evaluation threshold
param.help: Every protein is reported; this threshold sets the hypothesis behind the q-values, namely that the protein is correctly identified and its absolute log2 fold change exceeds this value. Triqler prints the minimum advisable threshold for the data in its log; values below about 0.2 are not meaningful.

param.label: Decoy protein prefix
param.help: Prefix that marks decoy protein accessions, for example decoy_ (Triqler's converters), DECOY_ (OpenMS DecoyDatabase default) or REV_. The job fails if no decoys match.

validator.message: Enter a non-empty prefix without spaces or quotes that does not start with a dash.

param.label: Separator between protein accessions
param.help: How peptides shared between proteins list their accessions: as extra tab-separated columns (Triqler's README format, MaxQuant and Quandenser converters) or joined by semicolons in one column (OpenMS TriqlerConverter, Triqler's DIA-NN converter). Triqler discards shared peptides, but only if it recognises them; with the wrong setting a shared peptide group is reported as if it were a protein. Detect reads the input and picks the style it finds.

param.label: Missing value prior
param.help: The default fits the censored normal distribution to all observed intensities. Use DIA for data-independent acquisition data, which fits it to the means of the missing values instead.

param.label: Minimum number of samples a peptide must be quantified in
param.help: Peptides quantified in fewer samples are discarded.

param.name: peptide_table
param.label: Output peptide quantification table
param.help: The peptide-level table Triqler builds from the input (its .pqr.tsv file).

param.label: Output protein expression posteriors
param.help: Raw posterior distributions per protein and run. These tables are large: roughly 30 kb per protein and run.

param.label: Output treatment group posteriors
param.help: Raw posterior distributions per protein and treatment group.

param.label: Output fold change posteriors
param.help: Raw posterior distributions of the log2 fold change per protein and pair of treatment groups.

tool.help:
## What it does
Triqler (TRansparent Identification-Quantification-linked Error Rates) summarizes label-free mass spectrometry data to the protein level and tests for differential abundance between treatment groups. Instead of filtering at fixed identification thresholds and imputing missing values with point estimates, it propagates the identification and quantification error of every feature through a probabilistic graphical model and reports posterior probabilities for the fold change.
It works with data-dependent (DDA) and data-independent (DIA) acquisition data.
## Input
A tab-delimited table with a header line and one PSM (or precursor) per line. The columns are shown aligned with spaces here; the real file separates them with tabs.
``` run condition charge searchScore intensity peptide proteins r1 1 2 1.345 21359.123 A.PEPTIDE.A proteinA r2 1 2 1.945 24837.398 A.PEPTIDE.A proteinA r3 2 2 1.684 25498.869 A.PEPTIDE.A proteinA r1 1 3 0.452 13642.232 A.NTPEPTIDE.- decoy_proteinA ```
- Intensities must **not** be log transformed. An intensity of 0 is treated as missing. - Higher search scores must mean higher confidence; calibrated scores such as Percolator SVM scores work best. - Decoy PSMs are required, and their protein accessions must start with the decoy prefix. - Every condition needs at least two runs, and there must be at least two conditions. Conditions are numbered by sorting their labels as plain text, so `10` sorts before `2` and upper case before lower case. Labels such as `1:control` and `2:treated` keep the numbering predictable. - Peptides shared between proteins are discarded. Their accessions are either extra tab-separated columns or one column joined by semicolons (OpenMS TriqlerConverter and Triqler's DIA-NN converter). By default the tool detects which style the input uses.
Triqler also accepts an extended format with `spectrumId`, `linkPEP` and `featureClusterId` columns for match-between-runs probabilities; see the [project README](https://github.com/statisticalbiotechnology/triqler).
OpenMS TriqlerConverter produces this format (Galaxy labels its output `csv`, but the content is tab-delimited, which is what Triqler needs). Gzip-compressed tabular input is decompressed before Triqler reads it.
## Outputs
**Protein tables** (a collection): one table per pair of conditions, named `1vs2`, `1vs3`, `2vs3` and so on, sorted as text (so `10vs11` comes before `1vs2`). With only two conditions the collection holds a single `1vs2` table.
Columns:
- `q_value` and `posterior_error_prob`: FDR and PEP for the combined hypothesis that the protein is correctly identified *and* changes by more than the fold change threshold - `protein` and `num_peptides`: the protein accession and the number of peptides used for it - `protein_id_posterior_error_prob`: identification PEP alone - `log2_fold_change`: expected value of the fold change posterior - `diff_exp_prob_<threshold>`: probability that the absolute log2 fold change is below the threshold - one column per run (`condition:run`) with the expected relative expression; 1.0 is the protein's geometric mean across all runs, and these values are not log transformed - `peptides`: the peptides used
Optional outputs: the peptide quantification table Triqler builds internally, and the raw protein, treatment group and fold change posterior distributions. The posterior tables are large.
## Choosing the fold change threshold
Do not set the threshold to 0 or a very small value. The fold change posterior always has some width, so even an unchanged protein spills over into small fold changes. Triqler prints the minimum advisable threshold for your data in the job's standard output.
## More information
See the [Triqler user manual](https://doi.org/10.1101/2020.09.24.311605) and the [project README](https://github.com/statisticalbiotechnology/triqler).
